# Handoff: the Prepare header's ⋯ menu, two groups

Written 2026-10-27 for a coding agent on `jusprin-newui` (at e72f5b8070). Untracked working note: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Read `AGENTS.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching anything outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.

## What was decided (Kenneth, 2026-10-27)

The "…" button at the right of the Prepare header keeps its glyph. Its menu becomes two groups separated by hairlines:

1. **This project:** a clickable project-name row, Version history, Export project 3MF…
2. **The app:** Preferences… (with ⌘, / Ctrl+,)
3. A hairline, then **Switch to classic view…** last.

Gone from the menu: the unclickable title row, Recent projects (its homes are Home's gallery and OrcaSlicer's File › Recent files), Back to Prepare (the Tab-key flip to OrcaSlicer's Preview is stopped at the shell instead). Not added: a gear glyph, Keyboard shortcuts, Report a problem (nothing in the app stands behind them).

Recent files, decided the same day: when JusPrin starts a project from a model file (STL/STEP/OBJ/…), that file's path is added to OrcaSlicer's File › Recent files through the existing `MainFrame::add_to_recent_projects`, regardless of the `recent_models` preference. A Recent entry must behave exactly like opening that file from the OS again.

The design is on the "JusPrin v2" canvas, https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, version `1793148288-e9fb`: board `main-10-prepare-header-project-menu` on the Main Page (under home-first-run) and the "In a project" stage of `prefs-13-entry-points` ("Where Preferences opens", Agent setup & Preferences page). The decision history is in `prepare-overflow-menu-proposal.md` beside this note.

## The menu as drawn

280 DIP popover (`component.popover.width`), rows 36 DIP, Body 14, on `surface.raised`; a separator is a 1 DIP `border.subtle` hairline inset to the row edges with 4 DIP above and below (what `HeaderMenu` already draws for `HeaderMenuItem::separator`).

| Row | Look | Press |
|---|---|---|
| Project name | Body Bold name, ellipsized; save-state word ("Saved", "Saving…", "Couldn't save", "Unsaved changes") as right-aligned Label meta; trailing chevron-right | Opens the Project tab of the Plates and Project pane, opening the pane first if it is collapsed |
| Version history | Body | The Project tab's Versions view |
| Export project 3MF… | Body | The same export the Project tab runs |
| hairline | | |
| Preferences… | Body, meta "⌘," on macOS / "Ctrl+," elsewhere | `wxGetApp().open_preferences()` as now |
| hairline | | |
| Switch to classic view… | Body | `detach_shell()` as now |

The two autosave warning rows ("Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry.", "Some older project data couldn't be removed.") keep their place directly under the name row, as disabled rows, exactly as `show_overflow_menu` inserts them today. The board does not draw them; the behaviour stays.

## Where the code is

Everything below is fork-owned. No OrcaSlicer-owned file should need to change; if one does, follow fork-stewardship.md and say so in the PR.

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp`, `StatusRow::show_overflow_menu()` builds the menu today (title row, Recent projects…, Back to Prepare, Preferences…, Switch to classic view…) and `show_recent_projects()` is the Recent list; both go. `project_summary()` stays: the button tooltip and four harness checks read it (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` 2449, 2522, 5625, 11057 compare `project_summary().BeforeFirst('\n')`); the new name row takes the name and the state word separately instead of the em-dash join.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.hpp`, `struct HeaderMenuItem`: `label`, `icon`, `detail` (right-aligned meta), `enabled`, `separator`, `invoke`, `title`, `keeps_open`, `decoration` (`HeaderRowDecoration`: `bold`, `trailing` icon, `detail`, …), `name`. A separator entry is `{}` with `separator = true` (see `PrinterMenu.cpp:18`). The name row is `decoration.bold = true`, `decoration.trailing = HeaderIcon::Right`, `detail` = the state word.
- `StatusRow` has no pointer to the pane. It gets callbacks from `ShellController` the way it gets `set_left_pane_toggle` (ShellController.cpp:650) and `set_agent_pane_toggle` (:319). Add one callback for the project rows, supplied by `ShellController`, that: expands the pane if `is_left_pane_collapsed()` (`toggle_left_pane()`), then calls `LeftPane::show_project()`, `LeftPane::open_project_view(ProjectView::Versions)` or `LeftPane::export_project()` (`Shell/LeftPane.hpp`, public). Do not reimplement export in the header; the pane's `export_project()` (`LeftPaneProject.cpp` ~148) is the one implementation.
- Back to Prepare: `StatusRow::request_prepare()` stays (slicing uses it); only the menu row goes. `ShellController.cpp:1526` picks "Back to Preview" for the printer panel's back label when the Preview tab is selected; once the Tab flip is stopped, check whether that branch is still reachable and leave a one-line comment either way.

### Stopping the Tab flip

`GLCanvas3D.cpp:3750` posts `EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB` on a plain Tab press over the canvas; `Plater.cpp:5185` (3D canvas) and `:5255` (preview canvas) bind it to `select_next_view_3D()`, which switches the Notebook page under the JusPrin header. The shell's `on_frame_char_hook` (`ShellController.cpp:1316`) handles only Ctrl+comma. Stop the flip in fork-owned code: bind the shell's own `EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB` handler on the 3D canvas's `wxGLCanvas` (`plater->get_view3D_canvas3D()->get_wxglcanvas()`) at install, without `Skip()` so OrcaSlicer's handler never runs (handlers bound later run first), and unbind it in `uninstall()` so the classic view gets Tab back. Alternatives need an OrcaSlicer edit; prefer the bind. Verify in the harness that posting `SimpleEvent(EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB)` to that canvas leaves `tp3DEditor` selected.

### Recent files

- `ShellController::take_opened_files` (`ShellController.cpp:896`) is the fork's "start a project from this file" path for model files (OS open, Home's Open…, drops on Home; a drop on the Prepare canvas adds and must not add to the list). After `add_dropped_files(again)` succeeds, call `wxGetApp().mainframe->add_to_recent_projects(from_path(file))` for each opened model file (skip `.zip`). OrcaSlicer's `add_to_recent_projects` (`MainFrame.cpp:4075`) already checks the file exists and persists the list.
- Open question, decide with Kenneth or leave out: Home's dropped files are written under `<temp>/JusPrin-dropped/<digest>/<name>` (`OrcaHomeBackend::open_dropped_files`, ~447). Adding those paths puts temp-folder entries in the list. Recommended: skip paths under that folder.
- A model-file Recent entry: `MainFrame::open_recent_project` (`MainFrame.cpp:4168`) calls `Plater::load_project(filename)`; `Plater::load_project` (`Plater.cpp:12164`) hands the path to the fork's `set_external_project_open_handler` (`ShellController.cpp:464`). That handler asks the "Previously opened file" question for any path, but an OS open of a model file never asks (`take_opened_files` does not consult `projects_for_source`). To keep "exactly like the OS", make the handler route a non-`.3mf` path to `take_opened_files({path})` and return its result; `.3mf` keeps the question. A missing file already gets OrcaSlicer's "The project is no longer available." dialog.
- Nothing else changes in OrcaSlicer's Recent files: no fork submenu, no path-to-project mapping, `recent_models` untouched.

## Tests, in `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (target `shell_integration_harness`)

- `verify_header_overflow()` (~6826) currently asserts the menu keeps Recent projects… and has no Version history / Export rows; invert it to the new rows (by window name: `_L("Version history")`, `_L("Export project 3MF…")`, `_L("Preferences…")`, `_L("Switch to classic view…")`, the project name) and that Recent projects… and Back to Prepare are absent. Add: pressing the name row shows the pane and selects the Project tab (`LeftPane::SetName` is "Project tab" when selected, `LeftPane.cpp:725`); Version history opens the Versions view; the two autosave warning rows still appear under the name row in the Failed / warning states (the existing `Couldn't save` checks at 11057 show how those states are produced).
- The classic-view scenario at ~11583 already drives "Switch to classic view…" through `choose_header_item`; it must keep passing.
- Tab flip: in a Prepare scenario, post `EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB` on the 3D canvas and check `m_notebook->GetSelection() == MainFrame::tp3DEditor` and the plater view stays "3D"; after `detach_shell()` the same event switches to Preview (classic behaviour back).
- Recent files: extend `verify_file_opening()` (~10022): after the OS-open of the cube (`m_plater->load_files(cube_files)`), `wxGetApp().app_config->get_recent_projects()` contains the cube path; the canvas drop does not add a second entry; then `m_plater->load_project(wxString::FromUTF8(cube))` (what the Recent handler does) makes a new project named "20mmbox-LF" with `prompts` unchanged (the reimport hook at ~10095 counts the question). Keep the existing `.3mf` reopen checks green.

Build and run on the shared Mac per AGENTS.md: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target shell_integration_harness -- -j4`, one build at a time, never restart a build to add targets. Each harness scenario runs in its own `--datadir`; see `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` and the mode flags near the end of `shell_harness.cpp` (~11950). Delete only your own harness data dir.

## Review points

- Only fork-owned files change (`Shell/StatusRow.*`, `Shell/ShellController.*`, the harness). Say so in the PR; if an OrcaSlicer-owned line had to move, say where it went.
- Wording: files are opened, loaded, imported or added, never "arrive".
- Every colour, size and radius through `ShellTheme`; no new literals.
- The PR description carries one line that a model-file Recent entry opens through OrcaSlicer's `load_project` and the shell's handler, routed to the same new-project path as an OS open.

# Prepare header: what the "…" menu holds and what it should hold

Written 2026-10-27 from the code on `jusprin-newui` (StatusRow.cpp, LeftPaneProject.cpp, PrinterMenu.cpp, FilamentMenu.cpp, ShellController.cpp, HomeUI App.tsx) and `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`. Untracked working note; not for commit.

## What the Prepare screen does

Prepare is the project window of the new shell. One header row sits across the top:

- Left: Home, and the toggle for the Plates and Project pane when that pane is closed.
- Centre: the printer-and-filament chip. Its printer half opens a menu (other printers, Printer settings…, Calibrate…, Add a printer…); its filament half opens the slot menu (filaments, colours, Use what's loaded on the printer…, Filament settings…, Calibrate this filament…).
- Right: the split print button (Slice / Print plate N, with Check Print, Print…, Print all plates…, Export sliced file… in its dropdown), the "…" overflow button, and the Agent-panel toggle.

Under the header: the Plates and Project pane on the left (plate rows with Rename, Arrange, Auto-orient, Lock, Plate settings…, Delete; + Add model, + Add plate; a Project tab with the project name and save state, Details, Version history, Export project 3MF…, Print history, Edit Project Info), the 3D canvas with the tool strip (Move, Rotate, Scale, Add instance, More = OrcaSlicer's right-click menu), and the Agent pane (chat, setup card, All settings, chat navigation, Preferences › Agent for setup).

OrcaSlicer's own menus stay on screen on every platform: the macOS menu bar (File, Edit, View, Window, Help) and, on Windows and Linux, OrcaSlicer's title bar with the same dropdowns plus Undo and Redo. The shell removes only the Calibration menu. So every OrcaSlicer command is still reachable, and the overflow menu does not need to carry them.

## The menu today

1. Project name with its save state ("Saved", "Saving…", "Couldn't save", "Unsaved changes"): a title row, not clickable. A warning row is added under it when autosave failed or old project data couldn't be removed.
2. Recent projects… (eight at a time, "Older projects…" pages on; opening one swaps the project in place)
3. Back to Prepare
4. Preferences… (⌘, / Ctrl+,)
5. Switch to classic view… (uninstalls the shell and shows stock OrcaSlicer)

What is wrong with it:

- The project name is a row you cannot click, and when the Plates and Project pane is closed it is the only place on Prepare that shows the name. The product definition says the name and save state are continuously visible, and that Project details opens "from the project name or menu". Neither holds today.
- "Back to Prepare" sits on the Prepare screen. It is there because Tab on the canvas still flips OrcaSlicer to its Preview tab under the JusPrin header (GLCanvas3D posts the tab event; the shell's key hook only handles Ctrl+,). Check print itself is a modal now, so the row is a repair for a leak, shown all the time.
- Four different scopes in one list: this project, navigation, the app, and an escape hatch.

I have nearly everything I need. The file is `prepare-menu-handoff.md`; the `.mdd` in your message was a typo. I checked every code reference in it against this checkout.

**What matches:**
- **The menu code:** `show_overflow_menu`, `show_recent_projects` and `project_summary` are in [StatusRow.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:488). The menu row type it describes, including the bold, trailing-icon and detail settings, is in [HeaderControls.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/HeaderControls.hpp:158).
- **The Project tab:** `show_project`, `open_project_view`, `export_project` and the `Versions` view are all public on the pane. The "Project tab" name it uses for checking which tab is selected is there too.
- **The Tab-key flip:** OrcaSlicer's Tab event and its two handlers are at the lines it names. The way to get at the 3D canvas exists as well.
- **Recent files:** OrcaSlicer's `add_to_recent_projects` and `open_recent_project`, `Plater::load_project`, the shell's handler for opening a project, `take_opened_files`, and Home's `JusPrin-dropped` temp folder are all there.
- **The tests:** `verify_header_overflow`, `verify_file_opening`, `choose_header_item`, the classic-view scenario and the four `project_summary` checks are all in the harness.

**What differs:**
1. **The base commit doesn't exist.** The handoff says it was written at `e72f5b8070`. That commit isn't in this checkout or on GitHub, where `jusprin-newui` is at `7963c4c53b`, the same as here. Line numbers in this checkout run 20–65 lines later than the handoff says, so it was probably written on the Mac against a commit that was never pushed. It doesn't block anything, but if that commit holds related work, I won't have it.
2. **There is uncommitted classic-view work in the same files.** The new `ClassicView.cpp/.hpp` and changes to `ShellController.cpp/.hpp` and `shell_harness.cpp` add a banner and a View-menu row for getting back from classic view. They also change `detach_shell()` and the classic-view test the handoff says must keep passing. My changes would go into the same files, so I need to know whether to build on top of that work or keep clear of it. That's the question in the box above.
3. **The build steps are for the Mac.** On this Windows machine I'll use my own build folder, not the main one, and the Windows build command.

**Still open, as the handoff itself says:**
- **Files dropped on Home:** should their temp-folder copies go into Recent files? The handoff recommends leaving them out, and I'll do that unless you say otherwise.
- **The "Back to Preview" label:** whether that code can still be reached once the Tab flip is stopped is something I'll check during the work.

I didn't open the design canvas. The handoff's table spells out every row, size and action, so I don't expect to need it, but I can check the board if you want the result compared to the drawing.

---
name: windows-build-machine
description: "Facts about the Windows Server 2022 machine used for JusPrin Windows verification (no admin, RDP at 100%, no GPU, toolchain and Mesa locations)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1e908987-3ebc-4e47-9372-ca2af82d4fee
  modified: 2026-10-23T15:13:22.028Z
---

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard has refused `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` in some sessions (reported as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. On 2026-10-23, in bypass-permissions mode with the user asking for the delete, `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` under `C:\b` worked. Build trees there contain a `src\Release\resources` junction into a worktree: list links first (`Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Attributes ReparsePoint`) and remove each with `[IO.Directory]::Delete(<link>)`, which deletes the link only, before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.

An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone
is not enough. Neither the Bash tool nor a PowerShell session started before 2026-09-16 inherits the user
PATH entry, so prefix `$env:PATH` explicitly in each invocation.

**Shared build tree (2026-09-17):** other Claude sessions build and commit from `C:\src\JusPrin` and
`C:\src\JusPrin\build` concurrently. Do not patch that checkout or build there from a worktree session;
a link there holds `.lib` files and breaks their build (LNK1104). Use a separate tree instead: configure
with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DSLIC3R_MSVC_PDB=OFF -DDEP_BUILD_DIR=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build`
at a short path such as `C:\b\wsh`, which is a full `libslic3r_gui` build of about 40 minutes. To symbolize a crash
without a debugger, relink with a `ForceImportAfterCppTargets` props file (Link `GenerateDebugInformation`/`GenerateMapFile`),
read the fault offset from the event log (Application, event 1000), and run
`llvm-symbolizer --obj=<exe> --relative-address <offset>` (the symbolizer ships in the MSVC bin dir).

- The in-app browser pane renders a `file://` page as a static snapshot and refuses `screenshot`.
  To look at a rendered page (e.g. a vitest `PREVIEW_OUT` page), serve the directory over a
  throwaway node http server on 127.0.0.1 and navigate to that instead.

**Commits can hang in the `entire` hook (2026-09-25):** `git commit` from an agent session in a worktree
never returned; `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` alone hangs too (60 s, no output,
stdin closed). `--no-verify` does not skip prepare-commit-msg, and hooks must not be bypassed anyway, so
stop after one timed attempt (`timeout 90 git commit ... < /dev/null`), kill the orphaned `entire`
process it leaves behind (`ps -W | grep entire`), and ask Kenneth. Other sessions' commits carry an
`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, so the hook works somewhere; the cause was not found.

**Concurrent harness runs collide on WebView2 (2026-09-25):** every harness exe uses the same WebView2
profile, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JusPrin2\EBWebView`. While another session's harness is running (e.g. a
long `--home-printers-live` fixture run), a second harness fails at once with
`shell_agent_page_handshake_complete FAIL`, and its app log shows `JusPrin agent page failed to load:
The group or resource is not in the correct state`. That is not a page or bundle problem. Check for
`shell_integration_harness.exe` in `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, don't kill another session's
process, and set `$env:WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER='C:\b\<tree>-webview'` for your own runs.

**Scripting on this box (2026-10-06; Python corrected 2026-10-21):** no `python`/`py` on PATH, but Python 3.13 is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\python-3.13.9\python.exe` and runs the prompt suites (`tests/project_prompt`, set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` and `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`). Otherwise use node (`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). Bash heredocs and `node -e "..."` that contain backticks, `${...}` or backslashes get mangled by the shell; write the script to a file with the Write tool and run `node <file>`. The main checkout's build tree `C:\src\JusPrin\build` (VS generator, Release) is fine to build from a session that is working in the main checkout: `cmake --build C:\src\JusPrin\build --config Release --target <targets> -- -m` after `vcvars64.bat`; harness exes there read `resources\` from the source tree, so `npm run build` in `AgentUI` is enough to refresh the Agent page. A touched `Workspace.hpp` rebuild of `libslic3r_gui` + `shell_integration_harness` takes roughly 10 minutes.

name: pane-build-and-gotchas
description: "Where the Plates/Project pane work was built and verified, how to rerun it, and the Orca traps it hit"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

The Plates / Project pane (handoff `left-pane-implementation-handoff.md`) was built fresh on `claude/open-figma-browser-86ed07` (commits 2742276f5f, 01610d3162, f12bff98a1); a sibling worktree `left-pane-implementation-handoff-d2959c` holds a separate uncommitted earlier implementation that was deliberately not used. Notes and captures: `agent-docs/jusprin/plates-project-pane-handback/` (untracked).

Private build tree `C:\b\opf` (configured with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DSLIC3R_MSVC_PDB=OFF -DDEP_BUILD_DIR=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build`); `C:\b\opf-build.bat <targets>` builds, `provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir C:\b\opf -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` provisions GL, put `C:\b\opf\src\Release` on PATH and set `WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER` when running harnesses. The Agent bundle was copied from the main checkout (`resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`, gitignored) so the default shell scenario can run. Scenarios: `shell_integration_harness --left-pane-capture <dir> [--dark-ui]`, plus the default mode (508 pass, 4 pre-existing failures that need POSIX read-only dirs).

Orca traps found: `GLCanvas3D::post_event` is async, so commands raise canvas events with `ProcessEvent`; `Plater::select_object` returns early when the canvas already holds the selection, leaving the ObjectList stale, so ObjectList commands (toggle_printable_state etc.) silently do nothing unless `update_selections()` runs first; objects load with `extruder=1`; a plate "has settings" only by bed type / print sequence / layer sequences / spiral mode, not by `config()` keys. See `orca-integration-guide.md` section 3.

name: native-ui-synthetic-input-and-capture
description: "Driving JusPrin's native (wx) UI on the Windows box with real pointer and key input from PowerShell, and capturing it — the four traps that each looked like an app bug"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 5f4606f5-f6a6-45fd-a91f-ea049831eb87
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:09:59.148Z
---

With the RDP session **connected** (see [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]] for the disconnected case), native wx surfaces can be driven from PowerShell with `SetCursorPos` + `mouse_event` + `keybd_event` and captured with `Graphics.CopyFromScreen`. Worked on 2026-10-02 for the left pane (`shell_integration_harness --manual-left-pane`). Four traps, each of which first looked like a defect in the app:

- **Arrow keys need `KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY` (flag 1).** Without it `keybd_event(VK_DOWN)` arrives as `WXK_NUMPAD_DOWN` (379), not `WXK_DOWN` (317), so a handler testing only `WXK_DOWN` looks dead. (Real numpad arrows send the same code, so handlers should accept both.)
- **The GL canvas takes keyboard focus when the pointer enters it.** Parking the cursor over the canvas between a click and a key press moves focus off the control under test. Park it inside the surface being tested.
- **Coordinates are virtualized, the screen copy is not.** PowerShell is DPI-unaware: `GetWindowRect`/`SetCursorPos` use logical units (screen reads 1728x1084 at 200%), while `CopyFromScreen` wants real pixels. Multiply by `GetDeviceCaps(DESKTOPHORZRES=118) / GetDeviceCaps(HORZRES=8)`.
- **Tab is not available for focus traversal**: OrcaSlicer binds it to switching Prepare/Preview, and `wxWindow::Navigate()` is a no-op in this wx build (`wxHAS_NATIVE_TAB_TRAVERSAL`). Fork surfaces must move focus themselves (the left pane does it in a `wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK` handler).

**Why:** each cost a rebuild-and-retry loop before the cause turned out to be the instrument, not the code. Same lesson as [[verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app]].

**How to apply:** start from a scratch `ui.ps1` with Click-At / Press-Key / Capture helpers built on the rules above; when a key "does nothing", log the key code in the handler before changing the handler.

Related harness facts from the same session:
- `workspace_adapter_integration_harness.exe` gets no runtime DLLs copied beside it; run it with `C:\b\<tree>\tests\shell\Release` on `PATH` or it exits `0xC0000135`.
- In the default shell-harness mode, `failed_autosave_is_visible`, `failed_autosave_has_plain_status_text`, `failed_autosave_blocks_project_release` and `earlier_model_version_available` fail on Windows on an unmodified build too: the test makes a directory read-only with POSIX permissions, which Windows ignores. Since the Check Print crash was fixed (2026-10-14, `20de313d92`) the default mode runs to the end on this box: 552 pass, 6 fail. The other two failures, `agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client_shrinking_to_1000_dip` and `growing_to_1400_dip`, also fail with the fix switched off, with identical geometry, so they predate it. The filament-menu keyboard checks (`down_selects_the_first_filament` etc.) failed in 1 of 4 runs of the same binary, and that run then stalled on an open setup guide. See [[windows-build-machine]].
- A baseline for "is this failure mine": copy `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\*` to a scratch dir and run that exe (copying avoids locking the shared build's exe).
Shell cwd was reset to C:\src\JusPrin

name: native-ui-synthetic-input-and-capture
description: "Driving JusPrin's native (wx) UI on the Windows box with real pointer and key input from PowerShell, and capturing it — the four traps that each looked like an app bug"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 5f4606f5-f6a6-45fd-a91f-ea049831eb87
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:09:59.148Z

With the RDP session **connected** (see [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]] for the disconnected case), native wx surfaces can be driven from PowerShell with `SetCursorPos` + `mouse_event` + `keybd_event` and captured with `Graphics.CopyFromScreen`. Worked on 2026-10-02 for the left pane (`shell_integration_harness --manual-left-pane`). Four traps, each of which first looked like a defect in the app:

- **Arrow keys need `KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY` (flag 1).** Without it `keybd_event(VK_DOWN)` arrives as `WXK_NUMPAD_DOWN` (379), not `WXK_DOWN` (317), so a handler testing only `WXK_DOWN` looks dead. (Real numpad arrows send the same code, so handlers should accept both.)
- **The GL canvas takes keyboard focus when the pointer enters it.** Parking the cursor over the canvas between a click and a key press moves focus off the control under test. Park it inside the surface being tested.
- **Coordinates are virtualized, the screen copy is not.** PowerShell is DPI-unaware: `GetWindowRect`/`SetCursorPos` use logical units (screen reads 1728x1084 at 200%), while `CopyFromScreen` wants real pixels. Multiply by `GetDeviceCaps(DESKTOPHORZRES=118) / GetDeviceCaps(HORZRES=8)`.
- **Tab is not available for focus traversal**: OrcaSlicer binds it to switching Prepare/Preview, and `wxWindow::Navigate()` is a no-op in this wx build (`wxHAS_NATIVE_TAB_TRAVERSAL`). Fork surfaces must move focus themselves (the left pane does it in a `wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK` handler).

**Why:** each cost a rebuild-and-retry loop before the cause turned out to be the instrument, not the code. Same lesson as [[verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app]].

**How to apply:** start from a scratch `ui.ps1` with Click-At / Press-Key / Capture helpers built on the rules above; when a key "does nothing", log the key code in the handler before changing the handler.

Related harness facts from the same session:
- `workspace_adapter_integration_harness.exe` gets no runtime DLLs copied beside it; run it with `C:\b\<tree>\tests\shell\Release` on `PATH` or it exits `0xC0000135`.
- In the default shell-harness mode, `failed_autosave_is_visible`, `failed_autosave_has_plain_status_text`, `failed_autosave_blocks_project_release` and `earlier_model_version_available` fail on Windows on an unmodified build too: the test makes a directory read-only with POSIX permissions, which Windows ignores. Since the Check Print crash was fixed (2026-10-14, `20de313d92`) the default mode runs to the end on this box: 552 pass, 6 fail. The other two failures, `agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client_shrinking_to_1000_dip` and `growing_to_1400_dip`, also fail with the fix switched off, with identical geometry, so they predate it. The filament-menu keyboard checks (`down_selects_the_first_filament` etc.) failed in 1 of 4 runs of the same binary, and that run then stalled on an open setup guide. See [[windows-build-machine]].

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
    
    SECTION("First scenario") {
        // Specific test case
        REQUIRE(obj.method1() == expected_value);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second scenario") {
        // Another test case with same setup
        REQUIRE(obj.method2() == other_expected);
    }
}
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Data Generators for Parameterized Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Function works with various inputs", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto test_value = GENERATE(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13);
    
    REQUIRE(is_odd(test_value));
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Range-based generators
TEST_CASE("Range testing", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto i = GENERATE(range(1, 10));  // 1 to 9
    REQUIRE(process_value(i) > i);
}

// Using variables in generators (requires GENERATE_COPY or GENERATE_REF)
TEST_CASE("Generator with variables", "[Algorithm]") {
    std::vector<int> values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    auto test_value = GENERATE_REF(from_range(values));  // Use GENERATE_REF for references
    
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Custom generators
TEST_CASE("Random values", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto random_int = GENERATE(take(100, random(-1000, 1000)));  // 100 random values
    REQUIRE(process_random_value(random_int));
}
```

### Test Fixtures
```cpp
class GeometryFixture {
public:
    Point origin{0, 0};
    Point unit_x{1, 0};
    Point unit_y{0, 1};
    
    mutable double tolerance = EPSILON;  // Use mutable for data that might change
};

// Standard fixture - new instance per test run
TEST_CASE_METHOD(GeometryFixture, "Point operations", "[Geometry]") {
    REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
}

// Persistent fixture - single instance for entire test case (v3.2.0+)
TEST_CASE_PERSISTENT_FIXTURE(GeometryFixture, "Persistent operations", "[Geometry]") {
    static int call_count = 0;
    ++call_count;
    INFO("This fixture persists across sections, call: " << call_count);
    
    SECTION("First section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_x) == 1.0);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second section") {
        REQUIRE(origin.distance_to(unit_y) == 1.0);
        // call_count will be 2 here with persistent fixture
    }
}

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests
template<typename T>
class NumericFixture {
public:
    T zero = T{0};
    T one = T{1};
};

TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE_METHOD(NumericFixture, "Numeric operations", "[Template]", int, float, double) {
    REQUIRE(TestType{} == this->zero);
    REQUIRE(TestType{1} == this->one);
}
```

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values
        CHECK(some_condition);
    }
    
    SECTION("Section B") {
        UNSCOPED_INFO("This survives beyond its scope");  // v2.7.0+
        CHECK(other_condition);
    }
}

// Warning and explicit control
TEST_CASE("Explicit test control", "[Control]") {
    WARN("This warns but doesn't fail the test");
    
    if (precondition_not_met) {
        SKIP("Reason");  // Marks the test as skipped (v3.3.0+, available)
        return;
    }
    
    if (critical_failure) {
        FAIL("Critical condition failed");  // Fails and stops test
    }
    
    SUCCEED("Reached successful completion");  // Explicit success marker
}
```

#### Static Assertions (Compile-time Testing)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Compile-time checks", "[Static]") {
    STATIC_REQUIRE(sizeof(int) >= 4);  // Checked at compile time
    STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(std::is_void_v<int>);
    
    // For traits and template metaprogramming
    STATIC_CHECK(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<Point>);  // v3.0.1+
}
```

#### Conditional Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Conditional blocks", "[Conditional]") {
    int value = get_test_value();
    
    // These record the expression but don't count as test failures (v3.0.1+)
    CHECKED_IF(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value > 0
        REQUIRE(value <= 100);
    } CHECKED_ELSE(value > 0) {
        // This block runs if value <= 0  
        REQUIRE(value >= -100);
    }
}
```

#### Benchmarking (v2.9.0+)
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance testing", "[Benchmark]") {
    // Simple benchmarking
    BENCHMARK("Algorithm performance") {
        return expensive_algorithm();
    };
    
    // Advanced benchmarking with setup
    BENCHMARK_ADVANCED("Advanced benchmark")(Catch::Benchmark::Chronometer meter) {
        std::vector<int> data = setup_test_data();  // Setup not measured
        
        meter.measure([&] { 
            return process_data(data);  // Only this is measured
        });
    };
}
```

## OrcaSlicer-Specific Testing Patterns

### Geometry Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Line operations", "[Geometry]") {
    Line line{{100000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    Line parallel{{200000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(line));
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(parallel));
    
    // Test with epsilon tolerance
    Line rotated(parallel);
    rotated.rotate(0.9 * EPSILON, {0, 0});
    REQUIRE(line.parallel_to(rotated));
}
```

### Configuration Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Config loading", "[Config]") {
    DynamicPrintConfig config;
    std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_config/sample.ini";
    
    REQUIRE_NOTHROW(config.load_from_ini(config_path));
    REQUIRE(config.has("layer_height"));
}
```

### File I/O Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("STL file parsing", "[FileFormat]") {
    std::string stl_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_stl/20mmbox.stl";
    
    TriangleMesh mesh;
    REQUIRE_NOTHROW(mesh.ReadSTLFile(stl_path.c_str()));
    REQUIRE(!mesh.empty());
    REQUIRE(mesh.volume() > 0);
}
```

### G-code Generation Testing
```cpp
TEST_CASE("G-code writer functionality", "[GCodeWriter]") {
    GCodeWriter writer;
    
    // Load test configuration
    std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/fff_print_tests/test_config.ini";
    writer.config.load(config_path, ForwardCompatibilitySubstitutionRule::Disable);
    
    // Test specific G-code generation
    std::string result = writer.lift();
    REQUIRE(!result.empty());
    REQUIRE_THAT(result, Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring("G1"));
}
```

### Performance Testing Patterns
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Algorithm performance", "[Performance][Algorithm]") {
    // Large test data
    std::vector<Point> points = generate_large_point_set(10000);
    
    // Time the operation (manual timing example; the BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto result = convex_hull(points);
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
}
```

### Custom String Conversions

#### For Custom Types
```cpp
// Method 1: operator<< overload (preferred)
std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Point& point) {
    os << "Point(" << point.x << ", " << point.y << ")";
    return os;
}

// Method 2: StringMaker specialization
namespace Catch {
    template<>
    struct StringMaker<MyCustomType> {
        static std::string convert(const MyCustomType& value) {
            return "MyCustomType{" + std::to_string(value.data) + "}";
        }
    };
}

// Method 3: Enum registration (v2.8.0+)
enum class Status { Ready, Processing, Complete, Error };

// Must be at global scope!
CATCH_REGISTER_ENUM(Status, Status::Ready, Status::Processing, Status::Complete, Status::Error);

// Method 4: Exception translation
CATCH_TRANSLATE_EXCEPTION(MyCustomException const& ex) {
    return "MyCustomException: " + std::string(ex.what());
}

// Method 5: Disable range iteration for problematic types
namespace Catch {
    template<>
    struct is_range<ProblematicType> {
        static const bool value = false;
    };
}
```

## Running and Debugging Tests

### Building Tests
```bash
# Build all tests
cd build && make

# Build specific test suite
cd build && make libslic3r_tests

# Build and run tests
cd build && make && ctest
```

### Running Tests

#### Essential Test Execution Patterns
```bash
# REQUIRED: Random order with assertion warnings (best practice)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Run all tests with verbose output via CTest
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure

# Run specific test suite with best practices
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Filter tests with specific tags
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry]" --order rand

# Filter by test name patterns
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "*geometry*" --order rand

# Exclude tests (negation)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "~[Performance]" --order rand

# Combine filters: (Geometry AND Config) OR Algorithm
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry][Config],[Algorithm]" --order rand

# List available tests, tags, and reporters
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tags  
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-reporters

# Debug failing tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --break    # Break into debugger on failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --success  # Show passing tests too
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --durations yes  # Show timing info

# Abort on first failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --abort

# Test sharding for parallel execution (MUST share random seed)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 3 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
wait  # Wait for all to complete
```

#### Reporter Options for CI Integration
```bash
# Different output formats for CI systems
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console     # Default human-readable
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter compact     # Minimal output
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter xml         # Catch2 XML format
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter junit       # JUnit XML (widely supported)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter tap         # Test Anything Protocol
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter teamcity    # TeamCity integration
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter sonarqube   # SonarQube integration
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter automake    # Automake integration

# Multiple reporters simultaneously (if supported)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console --reporter junit::out=results.xml
```

### Test Output Control
The custom `VerboseConsoleReporter` provides enhanced output:
- Test case start/end notifications with timing
- Section execution tracking
- Color-coded success/failure indicators
- Duration reporting for performance analysis

## Test Data Management

### Using TEST_DATA_DIR
All test data is accessible via the `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition:

```cpp
std::string mesh_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/20mm_cube.obj";
std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_config/printer.ini";
```

### Available Test Assets

#### 3D Models
- **Basic shapes**: `20mm_cube.obj`, `pyramid.obj`, `sphere.obj`
- **Complex geometry**: `extruder_idler.obj`, `ipadstand.obj`, `bridge.obj`
- **Edge cases**: `cube_with_hole.obj`, `sloping_hole.obj`, `small_dorito.obj`

#### File Format Tests
- **STL variants**: ASCII/binary, different line endings, Unicode names
- **3MF files**: Multi-material, complex assemblies
- **Configuration files**: Various printer/material profiles

#### Test Utilities
The `Test` namespace provides helper functions:
```cpp
using namespace Slic3r::Test;

// Load standard test meshes
TriangleMesh mesh = mesh(TestMesh::cube_20x20x20);

// Standard test configurations
DynamicPrintConfig config = config(TestConfig::PLA_default);
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

## Performance Considerations

### Compilation Optimizations
```cpp
// In CMakeLists.txt or as preprocessor definition
#define CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE  // 20% faster compilation, disables some features

// For faster test iteration during development
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION  // Workaround for VS2017 raw string bug
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

### Memory Leak Detection
```cpp
// For Windows builds - detects memory leaks
#define CATCH_CONFIG_WINDOWS_CRTDBG  // Must be defined for whole build
```

## Integration with CMake

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
add_executable(${_TEST_NAME}_tests 
    ${_TEST_NAME}_tests.cpp
    test_existing_feature.cpp
    test_new_feature.cpp  # Add here
)
```

### Advanced Test Discovery
```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
    TEST_SUFFIX " (auto)"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    EXTRA_ARGS --order rand --warn NoAssertions
    PROPERTIES 
        TIMEOUT 300
        LABELS "unit;core"
    DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST  # or POST_BUILD
    REPORTER junit
    OUTPUT_DIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/test-results
    OUTPUT_PREFIX "results_"
    OUTPUT_SUFFIX ".xml"
)

# Test sharding for parallel execution
include(CatchShardTests)  # If available
catch_shard_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    SHARD_COUNT 4
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}_shard: "
)
```

### Conditional Test Compilation
```cmake
# Feature-dependent tests
if (TARGET OpenVDB::openvdb)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_hollowing.cpp)
endif()

# Platform-specific tests
if(WIN32)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_windows_specific.cpp)
elseif(UNIX)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_unix_specific.cpp)
endif()

# Compiler-specific workarounds
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION)
endif()

# Fast compile mode for development
if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug")
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE)
endif()
```

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION
// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue
// REQUIRE((a <=> b) == 0);  // May not compile with MSVC
// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

// QNX/VxWorks C stdlib issues
#include <cfoo>           // Use C++ headers
std::foo_function();     // Always call qualified
// NOT: #include <foo.h> and foo_function();
```

### Catch2 v3 Features Available
```cpp
// OrcaSlicer is on Catch2 v3.11.0 - all of these ARE available:
// SKIP() macro                           - v3.3.0+
// Opt-in thread-safe assertions          - v3.9.0+ (NOT enabled here; see Thread Safety)
// Built-in BENCHMARK / BENCHMARK_ADVANCED - v3.x
// testCasePartial events                 - v3.0.1+
// Multiple reporters simultaneously      - v3.0.1+
// STATIC_CHECK macro                     - v3.0.1+
// Built-in test sharding (--shard-*)     - v3.x

// v3 notes to remember:
// - String matcher is "ContainsSubstring" (v2's "Contains" no longer exists)
// - Sections can still be re-run if a later section fails (unchanged from v2)
```

### Test Organization Best Practices

#### Project Structure Rules
1. **1:1 correspondence**: One test binary per library/module
2. **Hidden tests**: Use `[.]` or `[!benchmark]` tags for tests that shouldn't run by default
3. **Tag hierarchy**: Use consistent tagging scheme across the project
4. **File naming**: Follow `test_<feature>.cpp` pattern

#### CI/CD Integration
```bash
# Essential CI test command
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter junit::out=results.xml

# For coverage analysis
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter console --success

# For performance tracking
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --durations yes
```

This comprehensive guide ensures robust, maintainable, and efficient testing practices for OrcaSlicer development with Claude Code, incorporating all critical knowledge from the official Catch2 documentation.

content.text:
The ⋯ menu work is in, uncommitted, on top of your classic-view changes. Every new check passes on this Windows machine, but I haven't looked at the menu on screen yet.

**What changed**
- **The menu** ([StatusRow.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp)): from the top, it now shows:
  - the project name in bold, with its save state ("Saved", "Saving…" and so on) on the right and a chevron;
  - Version history;
  - Export project 3MF…;
  - a hairline, then Preferences… with its shortcut;
  - a hairline, then Switch to classic view….

  Recent projects, Back to Prepare and the unclickable title row are gone. The two autosave warning rows still appear directly under the name row. The button's tooltip still joins the name and save state with a dash, so the existing checks that read it are unchanged.
- **The project rows** ([ShellController.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp)):
  - The name row and Version history open the pane if it is collapsed, then go to the Project tab or its Versions view.
  - Export calls the pane's own export directly, without opening the pane. Opening the pane for a file dialog seemed like the wrong move, but it's a one-line change if you want the pane opened for Export too.
- **The Tab key:** the shell now takes Tab on the Prepare canvas and does nothing with it, so OrcaSlicer's switch to Preview never runs. When the shell is removed, it gives Tab back. Tab on the Preview canvas still switches back to Prepare.
- **Recent files:**
  - A model file that starts a new project (opened from the OS, Home's Open…, or a drop on Home) goes into OrcaSlicer's File › Recent files.
  - A drop on the Prepare canvas adds nothing. Home's dropped files are temporary copies, so they're left out, as the handoff recommended.
  - Choosing a model file from Recent files now opens it as a new project, like an OS open, without the "Previously opened file" question. A `.3mf` still gets the question.
- **One small change outside `Shell/`:** I moved the dropped-files folder path into a shared function in [OrcaHomeBackend.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.hpp) so the shell can recognise those copies. No OrcaSlicer-owned file changed.

**Tests:** I ran four harness modes:
- **File opening, classic switch, unavailable storage:** all pass.
- **Default:** six failures, the same six that fail on this machine without my change. Four make a folder read-only in a way Windows ignores; two are Agent panel width checks.

The new checks cover:
- the menu's row order, and that the removed rows are gone;
- the name row's look;
- the name row opening the Project tab, and Version history opening the Versions view;
- the "will retry" row appearing under the name when saving fails;
- Tab staying on Prepare, including after each return from classic view, and Tab switching to Preview while in classic view;
- the Recent files list, and opening a model file from it.

**Things to know:**
- **Preview can still be reached:** OrcaSlicer's Ctrl+R slices and switches to Preview, and with Back to Prepare gone, the menu offers no way back from there. Tab on the Preview canvas still works, and pressing the project name or Version history now switches back to Prepare first. I left a comment on the "Back to Preview" label saying Ctrl+R still reaches Preview.
- **The second warning row isn't tested:** the harness has no easy way to produce "Some older project data couldn't be removed.". That code path is unchanged.
- **Menu width:** the menu can grow to 420 DIP for a long project name before the name is cut short, the same as the other header menus. The board draws 280 DIP.
- **Housekeeping:** I rebuilt the Agent and Home page bundles, because they were older than their sources. I deleted the WebView2 folders I created under `C:\b`. Nothing is committed.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

- [JusPrin Windows parity handoff](jusprin-windows-parity-handoff.md) — handoff/capture locations, the 2026-09-09 root causes, what was merged 2026-09-10, and the three review findings still open
- [Windows UI testing without a desktop](windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop.md) — disconnected RDP kills cursor injection and capture; drive WM_ messages instead
